Maya: Quick update — ran an experiment with a dynamic-chunking background compactor on the KV cache while replaying long-context traces (~200k tokens).
Ajay: Nice, high level — did fragmentation drop? memory growth?
Maya: Short results: fragmentation index and mem growth both improved, but we saw a CPU spike during compaction windows.
Maya: Metrics snippet:
```
before: frag_index=0.34 mem_growth=1.42x p95_gen=12.1ms
after:  frag_index=0.11 mem_growth=1.08x p95_gen=15.3ms (during compaction bursts)
compaction_cpu = +28% peak on one host
```
Lila: Hmm p95_gen up ~3.2ms during compaction bursts — that's consistent with blocking merges. Was compaction running inline or background?
Maya: Background thread, but it grabbed a lot of allocator locks when merging many small free holes. We used chunk size cap = 64KB and aggressive coalesce.
Ajay: Can you paste the config you used?
Maya: Config we ran:
```json
{"compactor": {"mode": "dynamic-chunking", "max_chunk": 65536, "min_merge": 512, "cpu_budget_pct": 30, "scan_window_ms": 500}}
```
Lila: Two quick thoughts: (1) reduce max_chunk to 16KB for long-context workloads to avoid large scan work, (2) opportunistic merges only when cpu < 65% or latency SLO is met.
Sam: Also consider making the allocator record adjacent free-run-lengths (tiny metadata) so compactor can merge without global locking. That would reduce lock contention.
Maya: Good point. Right now allocator exposes free-list per-sizeclass; merging requires grabbing the master free-map. We hit contention there.
Ajay: What about fragmentation patterns? Were holes mostly small (<=2KB) or medium (4-32KB)?
Maya: Over 70% were <=4KB but many adjacent, so coalescing helps. However, small-chunk churn is high — reuse rate for 512B blocks is 0.9 reuse/sec which means compactor racing with allocation churn.
Lila: Proposal: adaptive block-sizing: keep 512B/2KB/8KB classes but add a "sticky" small-slab for hot slices that resists compaction for N seconds. Compaction only reclaims if a hole hasn't been touched for T windows.
Maya: We implemented a simple prototype: treat any free-run created within last 60s as "young"; compactor skips. Result: CPU down ~12% and p95_gen delta reduced to +0.9ms. Fragmentation slightly worse short-term but steady-state better.
compactor-bot: experiment/4770008765 completed — metrics uploaded to /artifacts/kv/4770008765/summary.json
Ajay: Can we see the artifact?
Maya: Link (internal): https://redwood-internal/kv/4770008765/summary.json — includes flamegraphs for compaction thread and allocator locks.
Sam: If flamegraph shows lock stacks in free-map::merge_range that's our hotspot. Could rewrite merge to be lock-free per-bucket then a lightweight global stitch.
Lila: Another heuristic: cap background compaction when overall host tail latency exceeds threshold. Eg: if p99_request_latency > 40ms then backoff compaction aggressively.
Maya: Agree. Also thinking of budgeted compaction with incremental in-place rewrite: limit bytes rewritten per second and prefer coalescing contiguous free runs smaller than X to avoid touching hot pages.
Ajay: Any perf regressions besides p95? IO, GC, or overall throughput?
Maya: No GC impact (we're native), IO stable. Throughput dips ~4% during heavy compaction but recovered. Not terrible but unacceptable for some SLAs.
Sam: Next steps: 1) prototype per-bucket free-run metadata to reduce lock scope, 2) implement young-hole skip window, 3) tune max_chunk down for long-context jobs, 4) add compaction backoff tied to latency SLO.
Lila: I'll sketch a config flagging system so ops can toggle the "young skip" and adjust budgets without deploy.
Maya: I'll run a second round with max_chunk=16KB + young-skip=60s + cpu_budget=20% and report numbers tomorrow.
Ajay: SG, thanks. If we can get p95 delta <1ms and frag_index <0.15 it's a win.
Maya: Yup — aiming for that.
Sam: Also add a microbenchmark that simulates long-context allocation churn so CI can catch regressions.
Maya: Good call, will add to perf suite.
Ajay: Thanks all :thumbsup:
